  • Strong customer relations skills including the ability to explain and train
  • Knowledge of proper use of hand tools
  • Knowledge of wiring and cabling
  • Analytical and problem-solving ability
  • Ability to follow prescribed company policies, procedures, and protocols for installation, service and equipment maintenance
  • Interact politely and professionally with customers and/or coworkers
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers, clients, and customers
  • Ability to effectively plan and organize
  • Follow all safety policies and company-wide safety requirements; encourage action assuring safe behavior; confront unsafe behavior and conditions proactively and positively
  • Work more than 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week, as required to meet business needs
  • Work in an unsupervised environment
  • Use a computer to communicate, create, and access data
  • Determine the priorities, goals, and objectives of work assigned

Physical Demands:

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.
  • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  • Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • Climbing:  Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.
  • Balancing:  Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.
  • Stooping:  Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.
  • Kneeling:  Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees.
  • Crawling:  Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
  • Reaching:  Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Walking:  Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
  • Pushing:  Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.
  • Pulling:  Using upper extremities to exert force to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Lifting:  Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.
  • Grasping:  Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Feeling:  Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
  • Talking:  Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Hearing:  Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.
  • Repetitive motion:  Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer.
  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures.
  • Indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.  Activities occur indoors and outdoors.
  • Extreme heat.  Temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour.  Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions, such as wind and humidity.
  • Hazards.  Includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current or exposure to chemicals.
  • Atmospheric conditions.  One or more of the following conditions that affect the respiratory system or the skin:  fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, or poor ventilation.
  • Oils. There is air and/or skin exposure to oils and other cutting fluids.

job.title: Local HazMat CDL Driver
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in Triadelphia, WV.   If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 


What's in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells, and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations.

  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain chemical inventory reports
  • Present a professional manner and work closely with salespeople to satisfy customer requirements.
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report field problems and/or safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Territory / Location Information:

  • This will be a local position that will be based in and will be responsible for chemical treatment and delivery within a 50-mile radius of Triadelphia, WV
  • Candidate must reside within 50 miles of Triadelphia, WV
  • Relief positions also available with a $2.00 an hour travel bonus

Schedule:

  • Multiple Schedules available
  • Monday Thru Friday with an occasional Saturday
  • Weekend rotation availability with days off in the week
  • 10-12 hour day time shifts

Basic/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED
  • Must be 21 years of age or older to operate company vehicle
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must have HazMat and Tanker Endorsements or be willing to be obtain within 30 days
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role
  • Must be comfortable working with cameras in the truck cab
  • No manual transmission restrictions

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, Porta-Feeds and mini/micro-feed units
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience in customer relations
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

Position Compensation and Benefits

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!

job.title: Senior Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Senior Chemist located in Odess, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


What’s In It For You:

  • Flexible, independent work environment where you will manage a monthly schedule
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology
  • Grow your income as you drive growth
  • Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and
  • personal protection equipment
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!

What You Will Do:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.
  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.
  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.
  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.
  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.
  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.
  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.
  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 5 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience, or
  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 3 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience
  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.
  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Demonstrated success working within a small laboratory team where collaboration, flexibility, and individual accountability are critical to overall laboratory performance.
  • Demonstrate initiative and ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks
  • Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and customer responsiveness.
  • Demonstrated desire and initiative to grow into leadership roles over time, including taking on increased responsibility, mentoring peers, and contributing to team development
  • Physically able to lift 50 pounds, climb stairs or ladder, and agile enough to squat and bend over
  • Ability to independently prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage a high-volume workload (handling up to 1,000 samples per month)


 

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Push/Pull/Carry up to 55 pounds chest high
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in oilfield production chemistry, chemical manufacturing, or industrial analytical laboratory environments.
  •  3+ years of laboratory leadership, technical leadership, mentoring, or senior laboratory experience supporting production chemistry operations.
  •  Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.
  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.
  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service.

job.title: Local HazMat CDL Driver
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in Williston, ND.  If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 

What's in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1
  • Starting pay of $28.00 - $30.00 per hour, with incremental wage increases through our Skills Progression Program.
  • $10,000 Hiring Bonus

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells, and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations.

  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain chemical inventory reports
  • Present a professional manner and work closely with salespeople to satisfy customer requirements.
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report field problems and/or safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Territory / Location Information:

  • This will be a local position that will be based in and will be responsible for chemical treatment and delivery within a 50-mile radius of Williston, ND.
  • Candidate must reside within 50 miles of Williston, ND
  • Relief positions also available with a $2.00 an hour travel bonus

Schedule:

  • Multiple Schedules available
  • Monday Thru Friday with an occasional Saturday
  • Weekend rotation availability with days off in the week
  • 10-12 hour day time shifts

Basic/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED
  • Must be 21 years of age or older to operate company vehicle
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must have HazMat and Tanker Endorsements or be willing to be obtain within 30 days
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role
  • Must be comfortable working with cameras in the truck cab
  • No manual transmission restrictions

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, Porta-Feeds and mini/micro-feed units
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience in customer relations
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

job.title: Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Chemist located in Cresson, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1+ years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience, or
  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1 year of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience
  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.
  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, etc) and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), with experience leveraging data management and reporting tools to support laboratory operations, decision-making, and process improvement.

Required Skills & Experience (Must – Haves)

  • Demonstrated success working within a small laboratory team where collaboration, flexibility, and individual accountability are critical to overall laboratory performance.
  • Demonstrate initiative and ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks.
  • Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and customer responsiveness.
  • Demonstrated desire and initiative to grow into leadership roles over time, including taking on increased responsibility, mentoring peers, and contributing to team development.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Physically able to lift 50 pounds, climb stairs or ladder, and agile enough to squat and bend over.
  • Ability to independently prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage a high-volume workload (handling up to 1,000 samples per month).

Preferred Skills & Experience (Nice to Have)

  •  Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.
  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.
  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service. 

Job Duties:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.
  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.
  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.
  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.
  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.
  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.
  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.
  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

  • Medium work:  Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • Climbing:  Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.
  • Balancing:  Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.
  • Stooping:  Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.
  • Kneeling:  Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees.
  • Crouching:  Bending the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine.
  • Crawling:  Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
  • Reaching:  Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.
  • Walking:  Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
  • Pushing:  Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.
  • Pulling:  Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.
  • Lifting:  Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.
  • Fingering:  Picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than the whole hand or arm as in handling.
  • Grasping:  Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.
  • Feeling:  Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
  • Talking:  Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.
  • Hearing:  Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.
  • Repetitive motion:  Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer.
  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.
  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures.

job.description:

What's In It For You

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching, and more!

 

What You Will Do

 

Packaging and Production

  • Operate packaging equipment including fill lines, pumps, valves, cappers, torque tools, scales, and labelers.
  • Package materials in accordance with batch instructions and production schedules.
  • Perform in process checks including quality samples for testing, weights, seals, fill accuracy, and container integrity.
  • Prepare drums, totes, and other containers for filling, labeling, and shipment.
  • Assist with equipment startups, shutdowns, changeovers, and minor troubleshooting.
  • Complete accurate electronic and paper production and packaging records.
  • Assist with hose line ups for transferring materials to and from tanks or vessels.

 

Safety, Health, and Environmental Compliance

  • Follow all site safety procedures including PPE, Lockout/Tagout, confined space, and hazard communication.
  • Handle and transfer chemicals safely in accordance with SDSs and site standard operating procedures.
  • Maintain compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, ISO, and internal environmental programs.
  • Report hazards, near misses, spills, or equipment issues immediately.
  • Participate in required safety training, meetings, and observations.

 

Material Handling and Logistics

  • Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, and drum/tote handling equipment.
  • Load and unload packaged goods and raw materials following site protocols.
  • Label, placard, and stage finished products according to regulatory requirements.
  • Support inventory counts, material identification, and documentation accuracy.

 

Housekeeping and Equipment Care

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area following 5S and housekeeping standards.
  • Perform basic cleaning and routine preventive maintenance on packaging equipment.
  • Participate in shift handovers, inspections, and audit preparation activities.

Pre-Employment Requirements

  • Must pass all pre-employment requirements as applicable.

 

Position Details

  • Location: Freeport, Texas.
  • Work schedule may include rotating shifts, nights, weekends, and overtime as required.
  • Work is performed in a chemical manufacturing environment.

 

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Ability to work safely around chemicals and operate industrial equipment.
  • Ability to lift 50+ pounds and perform physically demanding tasks.
  • Ability to wear required PPE including respirators and fall protection.
  • Ability to read, write, and follow detailed procedures in English.
  • Willingness to work rotating shifts, nights, weekends, and overtime.
  • One year of manufacturing or industrial experience.

 

Physical Demands

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Forklift certification or experience operating forklifts.
  • Experience with chemical packaging, pumps, valves, drums, and totes.
  • Experience with SAP or similar production/inventory systems.
  • Familiarity with ISO, GMP, or Responsible Care programs.

 

Working Conditions

  • Work performed in a chemical manufacturing environment with exposure to noise, heat, humidity, fumes, and moving equipment.
  • Required use of PPE including safety glasses, gloves, hard hats, and respirators as needed.
  • Work may involve climbing stairs, maneuvering heavy containers, and handling hazardous materials.

 

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, climb, and perform physical tasks for extended periods.
  • Ability to wear respiratory protection and other PPE as required.

• Strong knowledge of direct and indirect taxes, tax compliance, and tax accounting
• Experience with tax reporting, reconciliations, and audits
• Strong attention to detail and analytical skills

• Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities

job.title: Local Hazmat CDL Driver
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for an Operational Specialist located in Hobbs, NM. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


What's in it For You:

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!

What You Will Do:

  • This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations
  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Position Details:

  • Candidate must reside in Odessa, TX

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school graduate or GED
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must be willing and able to obtain Hazardous Material and Tanker Endorsement within the first 30 days of employment
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds

job.title: Undergraduate Engineering Co-Op
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

 

We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic undergraduate students to join our Undergraduate Engineering Co-Op Program at various ChampionX locations across the United States. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


As an Engineering Co-Op, you will gain valuable hands-on experience while supporting engineering, manufacturing, reliability, and corporate operations within our Chemical Technologies division.


If you are eager to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world business and engineering challenges, we invite you to apply. You will collaborate with experienced professionals, contribute to meaningful projects, and develop technical and professional skills that will prepare you for a successful engineering career.

 

Opportunities are available in the following locations:

  • Odessa, TX – Engineering Co-Op
  • Freeport, TX – Engineering Co-Op
  • Scott, LA – Engineering Co-Op
  • Evansville, WY – Engineering Co-Op
  • Sugar Land, TX – Reliability Engineering Co-Op (Corporate)

 

Specific responsibilities and assignments may vary based on business needs, location, and functional area.

 

What's in It for You:

  • Hands-On Experience: Apply your academic knowledge to practical engineering, manufacturing, reliability, and business challenges.
  • Professional Development: Gain exposure to engineering processes, project management, operational excellence, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Meaningful Projects: Participate in projects that support business objectives, operational efficiency, safety, quality, and reliability.
  • Collaboration and Mentorship: Work alongside experienced engineers, technical professionals, and cross-functional teams while developing valuable industry connections.
  • Career Development: Strengthen your technical, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills in a professional environment.
  • Benefits: This position is benefits-eligible in accordance with applicable company policies and program guidelines.

 

What You Will Do:

Depending on your assigned location and functional area, responsibilities may include:

  • Support engineering, manufacturing, reliability, and corporate initiatives that contribute to operational and business objectives.
  • Assist with planning, coordinating, executing, and monitoring engineering projects and operational activities.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support safety, quality, productivity, cost efficiency, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Analyze operational data, identify trends, and recommend opportunities for process improvements and performance optimization.
  • Participate in problem-solving activities, technical evaluations, and engineering assessments to support business decisions.
  • Assist with equipment reliability, asset performance, preventive maintenance, and operational improvement initiatives, as applicable.
  • Support project documentation, technical reporting, data analysis, and performance tracking.
  • Gain exposure to project planning, resource management, engineering processes, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute ideas and innovative solutions to improve operational effectiveness, efficiency, and sustainability.
  • Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and professional development opportunities.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to company safety standards, policies, and ethical business practices.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering from an accredited college or university.
  • Must have an anticipated graduation date of Spring or Fall 2027.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer immigration sponsorship.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Interest in engineering, manufacturing, reliability, operations, or continuous improvement.
  • Previous internship, Co-Op, academic project, or other relevant technical experience.
  • Exposure to manufacturing, industrial, engineering, or corporate environments.
  • Basic understanding of project management principles and engineering processes.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a professional environment.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to analyze data, prepare reports, and communicate technical information effectively.
  • Demonstrated willingness to learn, adapt, and take initiative.

 

Additional Information:

This Co-Op program provides opportunities to gain practical experience in a variety of engineering and business environments. Assignments, projects, and responsibilities will vary depending on the location, department, and organizational needs.

job.title: Principal Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are seeking a Principal Chemist in our Production Chemical Technologies – Production Maximization team located in Calgary, Alberta to develop products satisfying both business and customer needs with a focus on Production Maximization Chemicals.

The Principal Chemist will be responsible for performing and leading research, development, and problem-solving projects to enable new product development. The ideal candidate is highly versatile, communicates effectively, and thrives in a collaborate environment.

What’s in it For You:

  • The opportunity to take on some of the world’s most meaningful challenges, helping customers achieve their production goals through production maximization

  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth

  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers its employees through continuous improvement

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best

  • Comprehensive benefits package– medical, dental, vision, matching Pension Plan, and more!

What You Will Do:

  • Perform work in a safe manner while identifying opportunities for improving safety

  • Lead and execute innovation and technical support projects in the area of Production Maximization

  • Support the Production Maximization team on field qualifications

  • Design, conduct, and interpret laboratory tests to support key customer projects

  • Collaborate with other scientists and research groups on new development projects

  • Interpret experimental data and communicate results clearly to peers and project teams in written reports and oral presentations

  • Protect intellectual property, publish and/or present research findings

  • Work effectively in a team environment with cross-functional members

  • Provide consulting on experimental design, mentoring, and work direction for junior lab scientists.

  • Travel, including overnight visit to oilfield and customer sites.

Position Details:

  • The candidate must reside in Calgary, AB or surrounding areas.

  • Immigration sponsorship is not available for this role.

  • This is a safety-sensitive position, and the successful candidate will be required to complete drug and alcohol testing.

  • This role requires the individual to be clean-shaven to comply with safety requirements and occasional use of breathing apparatus.

  • Role is based on 40 hours per week and will require occasional travelling to oilfields and sites for customer support.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Education and experience should be at a minimum:

    • Bachelor’s degree and 7 years of industrial R&D experience; Or

    • Master’s Degree and 3 years of industrial R&D experience; Or

    • Ph.D. and 0 years of industrial R&D experience

  • Frequent travel to the oilfield is required; longer working hours are expected during traveling.

  • In-depth knowledge/experience in polymer chemistry, chemical engineering principles.

  • Strong project management and time management skills

  • Strong problem-solving skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Valid driver license and clean abstract are required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1-3 years of experience in oilfield chemicals, Advanced degree preferred

  • In-depth knowledge in polymer chemistry, colloid and interfacial science, chemical engineering principles

  • Strong understanding of test methods for emulsion breakers, reverse emulsion breakers, coagulant, flocculant and other water treatment chemicals etc.

  • Product formulation/development experience from benchtop to commercialization  

  • Demonstrated project management and organizational skills

  • Working knowledge of statistics.

Physical Demand:

  • Capability of carrying/lifting maximum 23 kg of weight

job.title: Senior Treasury Analyst I
job.description:
Responsibilities

  • Daily cash management ensuring timely funding, inclusive of daily projections & notifications for SCOT, MCNP, CAM ZBA & Offshore Pools as per Treasury guidelines & policies.
  • Perform FP27 reporting.
  • Define ideal working capital structure for each entity/country.
  • Prepare six months cash flow forecast monthly by country.
  • Analyze actual vs forecast cash difference to improve forecasting quality, identifying investment requirements by entity to be separately funded.
  • Maintain documentation on cash calls.
  • Monitor loan availability and advise ATs for increase of credit facility, FP9 follow-up.
  • Management and control of loans including interest, settlements, analysis, documentation availability.
  • Management and control of cash pools (FP33) including interest, rebalancing, interbranch analysis.
  • Provide monthly estimated LWD cash balance with comments for high/low cash balance and action plan (threshold to be defined with ATs).
  • Communicate significant change on loans, dividends, and initiate FX spot trade requests to be actioned by FX analyst.
  • Monitor volumes of transactions by bank account and flag inactive bank accounts to BAM for potential closure.
  • Place funding and FX request in eTreasury.
  • Process manual payments requests in RVND/EBS according to the business necessities.

What’s in it For You:

The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth.

The support of an organisation that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best.

Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers its employees through continuous improvement.


 

What You Will Do:

  • Maintain a tidy and safe working environment that meets the Goal Zero and Life Critical Rules set by the company.
  • Take an active role in Autonomous Maintenance ensuring areas are maintained in an appropriate state of cleanliness/order and condition.
  • Be able and active in making recommendations for improvements to practices and procedures in their area of work.
  • To be aware of, understand and display all Quality and Safety procedures to ensure high quality product is produced, shipped and received by the customer on time.
  • To be responsible for the safe operation of blending units on the Fawley site, ensuring quality, housekeeping and environmental standards are maintained at the highest level in accordance to company policy.
  • To be aware of the Permit to Work system on the Fawley site.
  • To be fully conversant with all safety and emergency procedures involving the Fawley Site such that they can become a member of the Site response team and know what to do in the event of an incident/emergency – Emergency Preparedness.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Numeracy and literacy skills are required, alongside a good attention to detail.
  • Previous experience in Plant Operations.
  • A team player who is keen to learn and able to adapt to changing scenarios while always maintaining and improving safety standards.
  • Forklift driving is a requirement and the specific training for this is provided.

Physical Demands:

  • This role requires working in a chemical manufacturing plant and is based on the Fawley refinery.
  • As part of your role, you are required to work a shift pattern that includes night shifts. You will also be expected to participate in the weekend duty technician rota as required by the business.

 

Preferred Qualifications/ Experience:

  • Previous exposure to operating chemical blenders and reactors processes.

job.title: Assistant Process Operator
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.


We are looking for a Assistant Plant Operator located in Odessa, TX. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.


What's in it For You:

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, technology and continuous education
  • Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and personal protective equipment
  • The opportunity to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth
  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives and ideas to achieve our best
  • Pride in working for a company that provides clean water, safe food, abundant energy and healthy environments
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k) with company matching and more!

What You Will Do:

  • Complete daily work functions within production operations in a safe and efficient manner
  • Blend, react, package, and transfer finished chemical products while maintaining quality standards
  • Operate mechanical and electrical equipment including pumps, mixers, automation control systems, and packaging equipment
  • Perform forklift operations to move raw materials, finished products, and packaging materials throughout the facility
  • Complete production documentation including production tickets, goods receipts, inventory transactions, and shipping documentation
  • Conduct daily inspections of equipment and work areas while maintaining housekeeping standards throughout the facility
  • Comply with all plant safety initiatives, environmental requirements, and quality procedures, including near-miss and incident reporting
  • Assist with physical inventory counts and maintain inventory accuracy
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable ISO requirements and company operating procedures
  • Work closely with Production Team Leads and cross-functional teams to support safe, efficient, and reliable manufacturing operations

Position Details:

  • Location: Odessa, TX
  • Department: Chemical Technologies Manufacturing Operations
  • Reports to: Production Team Leads
  • Ability to work the assigned plant operations schedule, including overtime as needed
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Must be medically qualified to wear a respirator
  • Physically able to lift, push, pull, and carry up to 60 pounds
  • Ability to climb stairs and ladders and perform bending, squatting, kneeling, and other physical activities required in a manufacturing environment
  • Must have the ability to safely work in an industrial manufacturing environment while wearing required personal protective equipment
  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role

Physical Demands:

  • May be required to Lift/Push/Pull/Carry up to 60 pounds.
  • Ability to climb stairs and ladders on a regular basis.
  • Ability to bend, squat, kneel, and perform repetitive physical activities throughout the workday.
  • Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment, including a respirator.
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Two-year Process Technology degree preferred
  • Minimum of one year of experience as an operator in a batch or specialty chemical manufacturing plant
  • Minimum of one year of relevant manufacturing or production experience
  • Forklift operation certification preferred
  • 24-Hour HAZWOPER certification preferred
  • Basic computer application literacy, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn internal business systems
  • Prior experience that demonstrates strong communication and organizational skills
  • Prior experience that demonstrates strong work ethic, effective time management, adaptability, teamwork, and attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment
